label: first copy-phase step after <DEL> echoing first token l (long sequences)
explanation: Fires only at step L+1 (recall_idx 1, prev input <DEL>), when the fed-back input is the first original token and that token is l (97% of activation mass). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases or at any other copy step. Magnitude and firing rate grow strongly with sequence length: rare at L<=6, rate rises from L=7 to L=9 and L=9 holds 56% of mass; top examples are all L=8-9. The second original token (out_tok) only weakly modulates (n/a/1 somewhat higher). Small residual (~3% mass) at step L+1 with other first tokens (n, w, k, 2). Precision is limited because many long l-first sequences stay inactive at that step (dev P 0.70, R 0.87, mass recall 0.95).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: l, n, w, k, 2, c; least: j, u, t, 0) and the next token to output (most: n, 1, i, v, a, j; least: w, g, -, b); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=10, L=8 & t=9.
